items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: Dick Allen would know his name instantly

ctx.x: He was dead in that two summer.

Well, yeah, the next summer, that was the fall of 1940, and he died in June. But he was talking how at that time he was still going to sue either MCA or he was suing ASCAP. He was always suing somebody for a million dollars, not paying royalties on his tunes. I mean, he had big ideas like that, exaggerated some things of that kind of, he wouldn't have been due a million dollars royalty, but he figured a lot of people were cashing in on his work, which they did. They never got to be millionaires, of course, but…
Well he said don't leave me here. He said he's always had six, seven, eight, or nine. Yeah, that's right. Yeah. Maybe they just gave him some.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: I don't believe Dick Allen got to see him. I don't even remember the details.

ctx.x: The early ones are not available?

No, at best. And also, I have a note here I noticed right here in front of me. I think the 1919 and 1920 files were missing, even in 1938 when I went there, in December of 1938. But I have some of these notes, which I'll go over, and might be able to enlarge a little bit on them. These are rather sketchy. Put on ahead. I mean, I'll send them down to Missouri. I see. Because it's a job that's going to take hours and days to go over that. And I'll copy it out, and it'll have to be by longhand, and I'll send a…
There's also a lot of material there that's invaluable. And we ought to be sure and get recorded some way.
